questions: Did progress rise above 0.155 on the s-bend and slalom, and on the oval above 0.11?
Did max_error stay below 0.069 on every track? If it rose, at what progress does the robot now leave the track?
Did line_loss_events fall to 0 on any track?
Did steering_oscillation rise with the lighter, faster-responding robot? If so, is the controller gain now too high?
If any run finishes, what is the completion_time, and is it still limited by speed or by the controller?

intent: Test whether lower mass (0.6 to 0.5 kg) raises progress on the s-bend and slalom beyond the iteration 5 gain, while keeping max_error below 0.069. Only mass changes from iteration 5. The sensor array, footprint, body, track and wheel radius stay fixed, so any change is attributable to mass and the speed it allows.
learning: Iteration 5 confirmed that wheel_radius 0.035 m raised progress without raising max_error, so speed is a real lever. Mass is the next test because its effect on acceleration and yaw inertia has not been isolated from body or track changes. If mass alone raises progress with max_error under 0.069, the next step is to test whether a small further mass reduction (0.45 kg) or a wider track helps. If mass alone does not help or increases drift, I will revert to 0.6 kg and test wheel_track 0.14 m next, which the Integrator set out as the next check.
rationale: Iteration 5 (wheel_radius 0.035 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg, track 0.12 m) scored 51.01, the best so far. Progress rose on every track where it was measured: s-bend 0.155 (from 0.15 in iteration 4), oval 0.11 and slalom 0.107. Max_error stayed below the 0.069 threshold on all three tracks (oval 0.0613, s-bend 0.065, slalom 0.0663), and line loss stayed at one event per track. The Integrator's pre-race rule said that if progress rises above 0.15 and max_error stays below 0.069, speed is helping, so the next lever is mass alone. Across iterations 0 to 4, sensor span, footprint, lead and body/track changes each left max_error almost unchanged, so the sensor layout is not the constraint. Iteration 3 lowered progress when body and track changed, so I keep those at the iteration 5 values. I change only mass, from 0.6 to 0.5 kg, to reduce yaw and linear inertia at the higher ground speed. I expect progress to rise above 0.155 on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error staying at or below about 0.069. If max_error rises above 0.069 while progress also rises, the robot is drifting faster than it corrects, and I will return wheel_radius to 0.03 m as the Integrator advised.
